legend: You are at a 1%%ZSMJ0%% dollar supermarket where there are n%%ZSMJ1%% sub-shops, each second a new customer comes in every shop, inititally all of them are empty%%ZSMJ2%%.
Since this is a 1%%ZSMJ3%% dollar supermarket there is only one worker. Each second this worker chooses uniformaly randomly a shop and serves all it's customers instantly.
To do some savings the boss doesn't hire extra workers unless all%%ZSMJ4%% the shops are all floaded. That is if we denote the number of customers of the i−%%ZSMJ5%%th shop to be ai%%ZSMJ6%%.
Then the shops are floaded whenever forall i∈[1,n],ai≥bi%%ZSMJ7%% for some pre-fixed bi%%ZSMJ8%%.
- Extra constraints : %%ZSMJ9%% we assume that b1=0%%ZSMJ10%%.
One may prove that the shops will be floaded almost certaintly, your task is to calculate the expected time at which the boss will have to hire extra workers.

It can be shown that the answer can be represented as PQ%%ZSMJ11%%, where P and Q are coprime integers and Q≢%%ZSMJ12%% mod 10^9 + 7%%ZSMJ13%%. Print the value of P\cdot Q^{-1}%%ZSMJ14%% mod 10^9+7%%ZSMJ15%%.
input: The first line of the input you will be given 1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5%%ZSMJ16%% the number of shops.
The second line of the input contains n%%ZSMJ17%% space separated integers b_1, ... b_n (0 \le b_i \le 10^{18})%%ZSMJ18%% and b_1 = 0%%ZSMJ19%%.
output: Output a single integer the expected time at which the boss will have to hire extra workers modulo 10^9 + 7%%ZSMJ20%%.
